Bug_Details: Duration.get() only works with SECONDS or NANOS. Duration.get(TemporalUnit) only works when passed ChronoUnit.SECONDS or ChronoUnit.NANOS. All other values are guaranteed to throw a UnsupportedTemporalTypeException. In general, you should avoid duration.get(ChronoUnit). Instead, please use duration.toNanos(), Durations.toMicros(duration), duration.toMillis(), duration.getSeconds(), duration.toMinutes(), duration.toHours(), or duration.toDays().
Bug_Explanation: The bug was embedded in the generated code by calling duration.get(ChronoUnit.MINUTES) which is not supported and will throw an UnsupportedTemporalTypeException. According to the bug rule, Duration.get() only supports SECONDS or NANOS when using TemporalUnit.
